edit.description: the install arm calls one library entry instead of sequencing discover, gate_verdict and run itself

the install entry builds one Discovery (with its bytes owner) and threads it through discover, the gate verdict and the placements; the ad-hoc Bytes::new() owners at gate_hooks_state/place_session_start/read_optional read through it
a gate seam that takes the caller's Discovery rather than building its own at gate.rs:567
the install index-count and paths-opened pins

summary: One `temper install` run passes the tree twice and opens settings.json six times: thread one tree index and one bytes owner through discovery, the gate verdict and the placements

per.section: Cost scale is hoisted, and pinned by count

acceptance: an install run (Represent::No path) passes the tree once and opens no file twice, pinned at the owners (import::index_pass_count, bytes::opened_since)
tests: install builds one tree index per run
install opens each file at most once per run

interface.changes: main's install arm calls one install entry that runs discovery, the gate verdict and the placements; gate gains a seam taking a caller-held Discovery
interface.hides: which owners an install run must thread between its three phases
interface.rejected: pinning through the CLI binary: the open and index counters are thread-local and never cross the process boundary, so the orchestration must live in the library to be counted

notes: Probed this tick over discover + gate::gate + install::run(Represent::No) on a one-skill harness with {} settings: index passes=2; reopened settings.json x6, SKILL.md x2, .git x2. A write through the owner reads back without reopening, so re-reads after a placement write still count against one owner.
